LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 12.3.1 POSSESSIVE PRONOUNS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.3: Language Use 12.3.1 Possessive Pronouns
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 12.3.1 Possessive Pronouns, part of Strand 12 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Which words do we use to talk about things that belong to you or other people?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 12.3.1 Possessive Pronouns together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving as the learner constructs sentences using possessive pronouns based on the role play with peers

● Digital literacy: Interacting with digital devices as the learner identifies and sign vocabulary related to theme technology

Values:
Responsibility: Hardwork as the learner takes up roles during role play activities.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Effective communication as the learner uses possessive pronouns in day- to- day conversations.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the knowledge of possessive pronouns to other learning areas such as Kiswahili and Kenya Sign Language
